summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against all eleven paragraphs of the selected working Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the difficult repentance/forgiveness distinction, the one-repentance assertion, the working positive reading in III.6, the salvation assurance, both denials that remarriage is sin, and the stated conditions for forgiveness. The simplified edition's shorter sentences retain these claims and their scope. Reader-facing servant and contextual repentance follow current policy. The notes disclose the substantive alternatives, conflicting edition reports, damaged or supplied Sinaiticus wording, and reported editorial conjectures without silently replacing the working readings or harmonizing witnesses. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied working source and accurate disclosure of the supplied reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or editions, certify exhaustive collation, or establish a uniquely correct interpretation.
